title: Enforce pure-kernel vs thin-CLI boundary across flagship crates (tabular, shape, rvl, pack, profile) for deterministic + wasm32 reuse
description:
## Problem
Several flagship library crates tangle pure domain compute with `std::fs::Path`, `clap`, wall clocks (`Utc::now()`), C `zstd-sys`, and ambient `~/.cmdrvl/state/witness` writes. Separating the pure deterministic kernel from the thin CLI shell guarantees reproducibility, enables in-process `cmdrvl` reuse, and unlocks zero-upload browser WASM (`cmdrvl.com/pack`, `/diff`, `/scan`).

## Scope
Coordinate and complete the pure-kernel / `fs`-free library boundary across:
- `cmdrvl/tabular` (`spine-rules/bd-nh4`: `open_bytes()` + `wasm32` check)
- `shape` (`shape/bd-8g1b`: `evaluate_bytes` + optional `cli`/`zstd` features)
- `rvl` (`rvl/bd-908`: `compare_bytes` covering numeric + overlap + `--non-numeric` + optional `cli`/`zstd` features)
- `pack` (`pack/bd-ztg`: `verify_tar_bytes`, `seal_to_tar_bytes`, in-memory `render` + optional `cli` feature)
- `profile` (in-memory `draft_bytes` / `suggest_key_bytes` over `cmdrvl_tabular::open_bytes`)
- Confirm already-clean kernels (`boundary-detectors`, `verify-core`/`verify-engine`) pass `wasm32-unknown-unknown` parity checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- All flagship domain kernels accept bytes/readers + explicit timestamps with zero `std::fs`, wall-clock, `clap`, or ambient witness access.
- `cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` passes across `cmdrvl-core`, `cmdrvl-tabular`, `boundary-detectors`, `shape`, `rvl`, `pack`, `profile`, and `verify-engine`.
- Golden parity test proves native CLI and in-memory library/WASM outputs match byte-for-byte.

title: Adopt fractal `control.v0` envelope, `--view brief|delta|frontier|full`, and zero-prose `refs.handoff` capsules
description:
Every workflow command in `cmdrvl` projects into the shared `evidence-protocol` `control.v0` envelope so agents use one uniform grammar from local checks up to portfolio runs.

Capabilities:
- `--view brief` (default, <= ~500 tokens): verdict, `boundary`, `coverage`, top-K `unknowns[]`, `budget`, `refs{}`, typed `next_actions[]`.
- `--view delta --since <prev_ref>` (<= ~300 tokens): turn-over-turn diff showing only newly resolved items, new regressions, remaining blockers, and budget delta.
- `--view frontier`: cursor-paginated slice of only answer-changing unknowns.
- `refs.handoff` + `cmdrvl handoff load <ref> --json`: content-addressed handoff capsule pinning inputs, boundary posture, and frontier cursor with hash drift detection for lossless multi-agent handoff after compaction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Consumes `control.v0` directly from `cmdrvl/evidence-protocol` (no forked schema).
- `--view delta --since <prev_ref>` deterministically computes resolved/regressed deltas and cuts output size >= 5x on iterative runs.
- `cmdrvl handoff load <ref>` verifies underlying input hashes and refuses with structured `E_HANDOFF_DRIFT` if inputs mutated.

title: Implement `cmdrvl orient --json` & fleet doctor: one-call cold-start posture, fleet health, active state, and typed next_actions
description:
A cold agent should never run 14 experimental `--version` / `doctor` probes to understand its workspace.

Implement `cmdrvl orient --json` (read-only, bounded <= ~500 tokens by default) returning:
1. `boundary`: live posture from `veil` / `airlock` (`enforcement`, `twin_mode`, `attestation_mode`, `local_reads`, `violations`, protected path/DB roots)
2. `fleet`: installed spine binaries, semver/digests, health status, available frozen profiles, fingerprints, registries, and strategy champions
3. `active_state`: running `twinning` instances, open `canon entity` sessions, in-flight runs, and witness tail hash
4. `next_actions[]`: ranked, typed actions with `effect_class` (`pure_read | twin_exec | broker_exec | local_write | external_io | irreversible_promote`) and structured `invocation {bin, argv}`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl orient --json` executes read-only in <250ms, never leaks secrets, and stays within ~500 tokens in `--view brief`.
- Degrades gracefully when optional tools (`veil`, `airlock`, `twinning`, `em`) are not installed, surfacing exact install/repair `next_actions[]`.
- Integration tests cover clean workspace, missing tools, active `veil` sandbox posture, and running `twinning` instance.
notes: 2026-11-25 Plugin Discovery: `cmdrvl orient --json` should also enumerate installed external `cmdrvl-*` subcommand plugins found on PATH (name + resolved path, querying `--describe` if available) so agents see both built-in and extension commands in one call.

title: Add core invariant, property, and differential verification suites (rvl math, verify portable vs DuckDB, pack/lock fail-closed matrix)

## Problem
CLI governance surfaces (`operator.v1`, `doctor.v1`) are mature, while core domain math and fail-closed invariants deserve stronger property and differential proof before building the `cmdrvl` wrapper and public browser tools on top.

## Scope
Add focused, fast invariant/property/differential test suites across core crates:
1. **`rvl`:** property tests over rounding, tie-breaking, zero-variance, NaN/Inf, overlap vs. exact alignment, and `--non-numeric` determinism.
2. **`verify`:** differential equivalence suite proving `verify-engine` (pure-Rust portable lane) and `verify-duckdb` produce identical verdicts and failure sets on all shared portable rules.

4. **`shape` & `decoding`:** zero-overlap key-viability edge cases and independent-channel corroboration / `resolve_liveness` invariants.

title: Add cross-repo E2E integration CI harness running real spine binaries on messy CSV/XLSX/Parquet fixtures
description:
## Background (Fresh-Eyes Architecture Audit)
Every `cmdrvl` repo currently tests itself in isolation with synthetic fixtures. Cross-tool seam bugs (`verify --lock` expecting `lock.input.v1`, `benchmark --lock` rejecting `blake3:`, `airlock` `messages[1].content` object format, `veil` `--explicit` flag gaps) slip past 16 green per-repo CIs.

## Scope
Add a cross-repo E2E integration harness and scheduled/workflow-dispatch GitHub Actions job in `cmdrvl/cmdrvl` that builds/installs the real spine binaries and runs the 3 canonical end-to-end pipelines on realistic messy CSV, XLSX, and Parquet fixtures:
1. **Tabular Spine Proof:** `vacuum` -> `hashbytes --algorithm blake3` -> `lock` -> `lock verify` -> `fingerprint` -> `profile` -> `shape` -> `rvl` (numeric + `--non-numeric`) -> `verify --lock` -> `assess` -> `pack seal` -> `pack verify` -> `pack render`.
2. **Boundary Plane Proof:** `veil` + `airlock` + `boundary-detectors` (verifying zero raw canary leakage across `veil`-authorized spine tools, `--explicit` flag denial, and `airlock gate` policy-proxy blocking/streaming).
3. **Twin Plane Proof:** `twinning --port 0` + `verify` + `pack seal` / `pack verify`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runnable E2E harness script/suite executes real compiled binaries end-to-end across all 3 canonical pipelines.
- Asserts zero canary raw-cell leakage in default (redacted) outputs, `lock.v0` (`blake3:` + `sha256:`) interoperability across `lock`/`verify`/`benchmark`, and `pack verify` exit 0.
- Wired into `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (nightly + `workflow_dispatch`).

A fetch step downloads, checks each archive against the release's SHA256SUMS (a mismatch or missing line aborts), unpacks into a work directory and records tag, asset, sha256 and `--version`. VERSIONS: nightly and manual runs use the LATEST release of each tool (the point is to catch a seam when it ships); `--pinned e2e/tools.pinned.json` reproduces a recorded set. Each run prints and uploads the versions it used.

HARNESS: Python standard library only (unittest), under e2e/. The repo has no code yet, and a Rust harness would need the one shared cargo slot. Runs locally (macOS x86_64) and on ubuntu-latest. Every tool call records argv, exit code, stdout, stderr and witness ledger (EPISTEMIC_WITNESS in the work dir; HOME pointed at the work dir so no user config or witness is read or written).
FIXTURES: synthetic only, small, committed, with the generator beside them: a messy CSV (BOM, CRLF, quoted delimiters and newlines, blank and N/A cells, currency and thousands formats, leading zeros, unicode, duplicate-looking keys), the same table as XLSX and as Parquet, an old/new pair with known changes, and canary strings no real data could contain. Also the bead's lock.v0 blake3: + sha256: interoperability across lock, verify and benchmark.

Every leakage assertion has a planted positive control: the same detector on the same kind of stream with a canary really present must FAIL (for example the tool's own --explicit output, or a planted line).

Each becomes (a) a minimal repro, (b) a bead in the owning repo after a duplicate check, and (c) an explicitly named known failure in e2e/known_failures.json tied to that bead id, which asserts the CURRENT wrong behaviour exactly: the suite reports it by name on every run, and FAILS if the behaviour changes in either direction (including a fix), so the entry must then be retired. title: Universal "did it change?" drop-in diff mode for cmdrvl diff (multi-sheet XLSX, unlabeled prior matching, and format auto-dispatch)
description:
Add a zero-config "did it change?" drop-in workflow to `cmdrvl diff` (`cmdrvl diff <old> <new>` and `cmdrvl diff --against <lock.v0|dir> <new>`) that answers whether a newly dropped workbook, dataset, document, or folder actually changed — and where/how much — in one redacted-by-default call.

Motivated directly by pre-wrapper testing on real 50+ tab Excel workbooks with multi-row title banners, renumbered tabs, and mixed row additions where running raw per-sheet `shape`/`rvl` manually requires ~100 invocations.

4-tier deterministic fast path:
0. Byte identity (`hashbytes` BLAKE3): identical bytes return `UNCHANGED` (exit 0) immediately without parsing.
1. Container/sheet inventory & unlabeled prior matching:
   - Multi-sheet `.xlsx`/`.xls`: enumerate sheets, report added/removed tabs, and deterministically pair renumbered/renamed tabs (e.g. stripping leading numeric prefixes or matching via `fingerprint` structure).
   - Unlabeled drop-in (`--against <lock.v0|dir>`): resolve predecessor by normalized filename stem or `fingerprint` template match; refuse with typed `E_AMBIGUOUS_PREDECESSOR` + ranked candidates if ambiguous.
2. Format-aware auto-normalize & diff per changed unit:
   - Multi-sheet workbooks: auto-detect preamble rows (`fingerprint peek` -> `profile slice`), infer viable key (`profile suggest-key`), and run `shape` + `rvl --key-mode overlap --non-numeric` per tab; degrade gracefully to row/schema counts on unkeyed tabs rather than aborting the whole workbook sweep.
   - Tabular files (CSV/TSV/Parquet/JSONL): `shape` + `rvl` (numeric + `--non-numeric`).
   - Prose/HTML/Markdown/XML: dispatch to `redline` (`cmdrvl-redline` plugin) when available.
   - Directories: `vacuum` + `hashbytes` + `lock` diff, dispatching each changed file by format.
3. Compact redacted executive summary & optional sealing:
   - Headline verdict (`UNCHANGED` | `FORMATTING_ONLY` | `CHANGED` | `RESTRUCTURED`), aggregate counts (tabs/files checked, unchanged, added/removed, net row delta, schema shifts, field/text churn), and top-K changed units ranked by magnitude.
   - Strictly redacted by default (zero raw cell/prose content unless `--explicit`); supports `--sheet <name>` drill-down and `--seal` to emit a `pack verify`-clean bundle + dossier.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl diff old.xlsx new.xlsx --json` sweeps multi-sheet workbooks with title banners, renumbered tabs, and added rows in one command without aborting the sweep on per-sheet E_ROWCOUNT/E_MIXED_TYPES.
- Identical bytes short-circuit at Tier 0 (`UNCHANGED`, exit 0) without parsing sheets.
- `--against <lock.v0|dir>` matches an unlabeled drop-in artifact to its prior version or emits typed `E_AMBIGUOUS_PREDECESSOR` with candidate list.
- Auto-dispatches tabular files to `shape`+`rvl`, prose/HTML/Markdown to `redline` (when installed), and directories via `vacuum`+`hashbytes`+`lock`.
- Default output leaks zero canary cell/prose strings; `--explicit` reveals details; `--seal` produces a `pack verify`-passing pack.

Only airlock is RFC 8785. lock and pack write 'sorted compact JSON' (keys sorted by Rust String order = UTF-8/code-point order, serde_json number text) and their stored lock_hash / pack_id depend on exactly those bytes. The two differ for e.g. keys mixing U+E000..U+FFFF with U+10000+ and for floats like 1.0 / 1e21. So core ships BOTH, with names that cannot be confused; switching lock/pack to JCS would change hashes and is NOT proposed.
2. Keyed redaction has FOUR different framings: rvl = HMAC(raw bytes; row key tuples u64-LE length framed); profile + fingerprint = HMAC(kind NUL text); verify = HMAC(serde_json text of the value); benchmark = HMAC(JSON string of the cell) printed 'hmac-sha256:'+32 hex; decoding = HMAC(canonical text) printed 'hmac-sha256:'+FULL 64 hex. Prefix 'redacted:hmac-sha256:'+32 hex is shared by rvl/profile/fingerprint/verify. Ordinal letters also collide: 'k' = row key (rvl, verify) but metadata_key (fingerprint).
3. Error code drift: the bead says E_REDACTION_KEY; rvl/profile/fingerprint/benchmark/decoding use E_REDACTION_KEY_INVALID; verify uses E_REDACTION_KEY. Core will NOT hard-code a refusal code: it returns KeyError{Empty,TooShort} and each tool maps it. Please rule on one family code before migration.
4. The CMDRVL_REDACTION_KEY fallback in the bead is NEW behaviour (no tool reads it today).

CRATE: cmdrvl-core, edition 2024, MIT, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. NO std::fs, std::env, clock, RNG, clap, threads, async. Callers pass bytes. Modules:
- jcs: to_string(&Value) -> Result<String, JcsError>; to_vec(..) -> Result<Vec<u8>, JcsError>; to_string_exact_integers(&Value) -> String (not RFC 8785 for |int| > 2^53); format_f64(f64) -> Option<String>. Semantics = airlock's jcs.rs (ported, provenance noted in the file); JcsError{pointer, number}.
- sorted_compact (the lock/pack legacy form, deliberately NOT called canonical/jcs): to_string(&Value) -> String, to_vec.
- hash: enum Algorithm{Blake3,Sha256}; Algorithm::of(prefixed)->Option (prefix only = spine-rules semantics); hash_bytes(Algorithm,&[u8]) -> String ('<alg>:<lower hex>'); parse_prefixed(&str) -> Result<(Algorithm,&str), HashError> (STRICT: known prefix + exactly 64 lowercase hex; new, stricter than any tool today, for new callers only).
- lockfile: parse(&str) -> Result<LockV0, LockRefusal>; candidates(); verify_member(&LockV0, path, bytes) -> Result<MemberVerdict, LockRefusal> = spine-rules::lockfile semantics UNCHANGED (exact path else unique basename; hash with the member's own algorithm; unknown algorithm refused; drift decided by string equality). - NO DEPENDENCY CYCLE: core depends on nothing from spine-rules. Later spine-rules may depend on core and re-export lockfile; the copied conformance cases are what keeps them equal until then.
- refusal: enum ExitCode{Positive=0, Negative=1, Refusal=2, Policy=3} (spine ADR); struct Refusal{code: String, message: String, detail: Value, next_command: Option<String>} and Envelope{version, outcome:'REFUSAL', refusal} with to_json() = sorted_compact (lock's to_json behaviour). Codes stay tool-owned strings.
- contract: ContractHash newtype over a strictly parsed prefixed hash, ContractHash::of_jcs(&Value) = blake3 over JCS (airlock's jcs_blake3_hash). NOTE: no tool has a ContractHash type today; this is a proposal for review, not a unification.
- redact (see byte rules below): RedactionKey::new(Vec<u8>) -> Result<_, KeyError> (empty -> Empty, <16 bytes -> TooShort; Debug prints <withheld>); RedactionKey::from_optional(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<_>>; select_key(tool_var: Option<&[u8]>, fallback: Option<&[u8]>) where a SET tool var always wins and fails closed (never falls through to the fallback, never to ordinals); constants MIN_KEY_BYTES=16, FALLBACK_ENV='CMDRVL_REDACTION_KEY' (a name only; core reads no environment); key.hmac_sha256(&[u8]) -> [u8;32]; key.marker_raw(bytes) and key.marker_tagged(tag, bytes); frame_components(parts) ; struct Namespace{tag:&'static str, letter:char} with ROW(k) VALUE(v) COLUMN(c) SHEET(s) HEADING(h) PATH(p) METADATA_KEY(k) OUTLINE(o) NAMESPACE(n); enum Scheme{Raw, Tagged}; Marker::ordinal(), Marker::keyed(&key, Scheme); mark(ns, bytes) -> String; ordinal(ns, bytes) -> usize for callers with their own text format.
EXACT BYTES: marker = 'redacted:hmac-sha256:' + lowercase hex of the FIRST 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(key, input). Raw: input = bytes as given (rvl: cell bytes, column-name bytes; for a row key, frame_components = for each component u64 little-endian length then the bytes, concatenated). Tagged: input = tag bytes, one 0x00, text bytes (profile 'column'; fingerprint column/sheet/heading/path/metadata_key/outline/namespace). Raw has no domain separation (rvl's documented behaviour, kept byte for byte); Tagged does. Ordinal: 'redacted:ref:<letter><n>', n from 1 per Namespace in first-appearance order, equal bytes share a ref, no hash computed. verify = Raw over serde_json text of the value. benchmark/decoding formats are reachable with hmac_sha256() + their own prefix; core adds no second marker format.

- Redaction, verify-cli redact.rs -> core redact: key rule and KeyError (:44, :71; same reasons empty/too_short, same 16-byte minimum) -> RedactionKey::from_optional; keyed marker (:93) -> marker_raw over the SAME serde_json text; ordinals (:111-150) -> Marker::ordinal with Namespace::ROW (k) and VALUE (v).   gold.jsonl   {"entity": "1", "field": "balance", "expected": "2", "compare_as": "number"}
  claims.jsonl {"claim_id": "c1", "source": "input", "quote": "loan_id", "byte_span": {"start": 0, "end": 7}}

  shape loans.csv loans.csv --key loan_id --json --no-witness
  rvl loans.csv loans.csv --key loan_id --json --no-witness
  benchmark loans.csv --assertions gold.jsonl --key loan_id --json --no-witness
  verify run rules.verify.json --bind input=loans.csv --json --no-witness

Correction to my earlier two-period example, in which verify passed and shape refused: that input was matched by file name only. It does not show that shape is safe from this. verify's README warning (added for bd-6nk) speaks only of verify; I did not change it.

== SCOPE ==
Match an input against lock members: shape, rvl, benchmark, verify run, verify ground.
No change needed: lock (creation does no input matching; lock verify checks every member against files under a root), pack (matches only its own manifest), airlock (found no input-lock reading; my search hit was the string airlock.v0).
Sources read at: shape 8f52dee, rvl 976340c, benchmark fec0478, lock 09805c6, pack 5c319ca, airlock 4d68d60, verify 980aa50. Binaries run: the released versions above, x86_64 macOS. shape main has added a lock receipt since 0.10.1 (bd-9pck); its matching loop is unchanged in the diff I read.

Current rules, from source:
- shape, rvl, benchmark: exact path first (typed name with \ turned into /), else platform file name. By file name, two or more distinct (lock, path) entries are ambiguous. Among the entries used, ANY matching digest passes.
- verify run and ground: trim, strip one leading ./, strip trailing separators, on both sides; \ also separates file names. By file name, ambiguous only if the distinct member PATHS differ across all locks. ANY matching digest passes.
- The doc comment on run's candidates() says it is the same rule as shape, rvl and benchmark. It is not. Unchanged.

== PROPOSED RULE (R1, recommended) ==
Per input, from names and digests only:
1. Drop every leading "./" from the typed name and from each member path. No trimming, no trailing-separator removal. "\" is an ordinary character in the rule; a Windows caller converts the typed name to "/" before calling.
2. Candidates: members whose path equals the name. If none, members whose last "/" segment equals the name's non-empty last segment, and these must all have one path.
3. Every candidate digest must be usable.
4. EVERY candidate digest must equal the input's digest for its algorithm.
A file set is accepted only if each input is. Loading and validation stay per tool and unchanged (versions, run's legacy lock.input.v1, required fields, ground's whole-lock digest check). Only matching changes.

== INTERFACE (names and digests only; no file access) ==
  struct Member<'a>    { lock: usize /* position among the --lock arguments */, path: &'a str, digest: &'a str }
  enum   Basis         { ExactPath, FileName }
  struct Selection<'a> { basis: Basis, candidates: Vec<Member<'a>> /* non-empty, one normalized path, in lock then member order */ }
  enum   SelectError<'a> { NotListed, SeveralPaths(Vec<Member<'a>>), UnusableDigest(Member<'a>) }
  fn select(input_name, members) -> Result<Selection, SelectError>
  fn Selection::algorithms()     -> the algorithms the caller must hash the input with
  fn Selection::judge(observed: (algorithm, digest) pairs) -> Result<Verdict, MissingDigest>
  enum Verdict<'a> { Verified { locks: Vec<usize>, matched: Vec<Member<'a>> },
                     Drift    { matching_locks: Vec<usize>, matched: Vec<Member<'a>>, differing: Vec<Member<'a>> } }
Verified.locks is EVERY lock that matched; Drift also says which locks matched and which entries differ. A lock passed twice has two positions; the caller de-duplicates for its report (verify names locks by file name today). The caller keeps all reading and streaming hashing. It would be a new function in cmdrvl-core: today's core::lockfile is a different thing (takes bytes, gives no lock position, refuses lock.input.v1, checks the whole lock).
Report output: keep what each tool prints for a pass today (verify lists every vouching lock; shape's new receipt, rvl and benchmark name the first matching one). Listing all of them in those three is a separate output change to approve.

== REFUSAL CODES ==
- NotListed, SeveralPaths: E_INPUT_NOT_LOCKED.
- UnusableDigest: each tool keeps its current code (from source: shape and rvl treat it as a lock-file I/O failure, benchmark has E_UNSUPPORTED_HASH_ALGORITHM; verify keeps what it uses now). My matrix grouped these codes together, so it does not show them separately. Change: it is checked for all candidates before any match, so lock order no longer matters.
- Drift, whether no candidate or only some match: E_INPUT_DRIFT; "expected" is the first differing entry. Recommended over a new conflict code. Naming every disagreeing lock in the detail would be an added output field, to approve separately.
Code changes between two refusals are not counted below. Example: two locks with the same name and different digests matched by file name are E_INPUT_NOT_LOCKED today in shape, rvl and benchmark, and would be E_INPUT_DRIFT.

== CHANGED ACCEPT/REFUSE SETS: GENERATED SPACE ==
Space: 4 typed names (loans.csv, ./loans.csv, d/loans.csv, ./d/loans.csv) x 300 lock layouts: one entry (12), two entries in one lock (144), or one entry in each of two locks (144). Entry = one of 6 paths (loans.csv, ./loans.csv, d/loans.csv, e/loans.csv, e\loans.csv, other.csv) x a digest that matches the input ("match") or does not ("other"). 1,200 cases, plus 13 targeted spellings.
Check on my method: models of the CURRENT rules agreed with the released binaries on all 1,213 cases for shape, rvl and ground, and on all but one targeted case for benchmark and run (that binary refused the file format, so it shows nothing about matching). In the 1,200, shape = rvl = benchmark and run = ground, verdict for verdict. OLD verdicts below are observed. NEW verdicts are computed from the rule; nothing implements it.
Each class is a set; each example is one observed member of it. The case-by-case list is not in this comment.

shape, rvl, benchmark (same set for each): 33 newly refused, 77 newly accepted.
  Newly refused (released accept -> E_INPUT_DRIFT):
  - 10: candidates disagree, exact path, across two locks. Input loans.csv; {loans.csv: match} | {loans.csv: other}
  - 13: candidates disagree, exact path, inside one lock (entries with the same path after dropping ./). {loans.csv: match, loans.csv: other}
  - 10: candidates disagree, file name, inside one lock. Input loans.csv; {d/loans.csv: match, d/loans.csv: other}
  Newly accepted (released E_INPUT_NOT_LOCKED -> accept):
  - 64: need leading ./ ignored. Input loans.csv; {./loans.csv: match, d/loans.csv: match}
  - 13: one path in two locks, same digest. Input loans.csv; {./loans.csv: match} | {./loans.csv: match}
verify run, verify ground (same set for each): 156 newly refused, 80 newly accepted.
  Newly refused (released accept):
  - 20: candidates disagree, exact path, across two locks. {loans.csv: match} | {loans.csv: other}
  - 20: candidates disagree, exact path, inside one lock. {loans.csv: match, loans.csv: other}
  - 28: candidates disagree, file name, across two locks. {d/loans.csv: match} | {d/loans.csv: other}
  - 28: candidates disagree, file name, inside one lock. {d/loans.csv: match, d/loans.csv: other}

== EDGE CASES (targeted; old = released) ==
Input loans.csv and a matching digest unless shown. S = shape, R = rvl, B = benchmark, run, ground.
1.  sha256 entry matches, blake3 entry for the same path does not: all five accept -> drift.
2.  matching entry, then md5 entry for the same path: S R B accept -> unusable; run, ground unusable (same).
3.  md5 entry first: all five unusable (same).
4.  member " loans.csv": S R B not-locked (same); run, ground accept -> not-locked.
5.  member "loans.csv/": all five accept -> not-locked.
6.  typed "d", member "d/.": S R accept -> not-locked; ground not-locked (same); benchmark and run NOT MEASURED (format refusal).
7.  member "././loans.csv" plus "a/loans.csv": other: all five not-locked -> accept.

Released tools and real released locks. "Right" = files as locked; "swapped" = the two periods' bytes exchanged.
A. One lock over the parent folder (members dec/loans.csv, nov/loans.csv), run from the parent, bound by those paths: all five accept right and report drift for swapped. THIS IS THE SUPPORTED WAY; R1 keeps it (computed).

D. Same two locks, inside dec, bound loans.csv and ../nov/loans.csv: loans.csv is accepted by all five, right or swapped; ../nov/loans.csv by run and ground only.

R1 (recommended)                                       33 / 77               156 / 80
R1a: also refuse one path in two locks by file name,

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
DECISION NEEDED (orchestrator, 2026-11-28). Reply with a comment starting "ANSWER:". This does not block the verify release. It does block this bead, and cmd-3w7 and the beads that wait on it.

BACKGROUND (read-only per-tool check in the comment above; I spot-checked the import counts and local serializer lines, not the tests it cites). DONE: lock.v0 verification comes from cmdrvl-core in lock, verify, benchmark, shape and rvl (pack and airlock have no input-lock verifier). Canonical JSON comes from core in lock, pack, airlock and in the rvl witness. NOT DONE: (1) verify, benchmark and shape still write their JSON output and witness lines with local serializers; the check found that switching would change output bytes and witness ids, though not verdicts. That conflicts with this bead requiring zero byte regression. (2) None of the seven uses the shared Refusal, ExitCode or ContractHash types. The shared Refusal envelope has a different shape, so using it directly changes refusal output. The check found ExitCode could be swapped with no output change; ContractHash has no current user.

Q1. How should this bead finish?
 (a) Narrow the acceptance to what is done, never changing published output just to share code; close it, and move remaining type adoption to one low-priority bead.
 (b) As (a), but first swap ExitCode in all seven (no output change expected, still to be proven).
 (c) Finish as written: move the three serializers and the shared types in, accepting changed output bytes and witness ids in a planned release with release notes.
RECOMMENDATION: (a). The shared parts that affect correctness (hashing, redaction, lock checking) are in place; (b) and (c) add no behaviour a user would see, and (c) breaks stored byte comparisons.
NOTE: tools pin two different core revisions (lock, pack, airlock: a3dad0b; the other four: 9cdf14a). This question does not change that.
